Design: 4 temperatures (26, 29, 31, 33) x 3 weeks (1, 3, 5), n = 3 per cell -> 36 samples.
Mats were resampled across weeks but there is no mat ID, so samples from different weeks are not
independent and a Week effect cannot be tested. **Every test is run separately within each week
(12 samples, n = 3 per temperature, one-way Temperature models).** Across-week figures are descriptive only.

Flow per week (same as Summer / Field): rarefy -> alpha (unrarefied, single-draw, 100-draw) ->
beta (main = prevalence-filtered unrarefied CLR/Euclidean; sensitivity = purgeOutliers + 100-draw rarefied) -> ANCOM-BC2 (Class level, holm).

~set-up~
```{r}
# ---- read, remove 0 asvs across all samples, subset to Temp ----
ps.cleaner <- readRDS("CH4_ps.cleaner.RDS")
ps.cleaner.filtered <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps.cleaner) > 0, ps.cleaner)

dist.temp.git.ps <- subset_samples(ps.cleaner.filtered, Experiment == "Temp")
dist.temp.git.ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(dist.temp.git.ps) > 0, dist.temp.git.ps)

# ---- rename 7th column of tax table to sequence ----
tt <- tax_table(dist.temp.git.ps); colnames(tt)[7] <- "Sequence"
tax_table(dist.temp.git.ps) <- tt

# ---- metadata clean-up ----
sd <- data.frame(sample_data(dist.temp.git.ps))
sd$is.neg <- NULL
unique(sd$Temperature); unique(sd$Week)     # check raw labels before factoring

sd$Temperature <- factor(sd$Temperature, levels = c("26","29","31","33"))
sd$Temp_num    <- as.numeric(as.character(sd$Temperature))   # for linear-trend models
# handles "1", "Week 1", "W1", 1 ... -> "1"
sd$Week <- factor(readr::parse_number(as.character(sd$Week)), levels = c(1, 3, 5))
stopifnot(!anyNA(sd$Temperature), !anyNA(sd$Week))
sd$Temperature <- droplevels(sd$Temperature)
sd$Week        <- droplevels(sd$Week)
sample_data(dist.temp.git.ps) <- sample_data(sd)

nsamples(dist.temp.git.ps)
ntaxa(dist.temp.git.ps)

# ---- samples per treatment ----
table(sd$Temperature, sd$Week)        # should be 3 in every cell

# ---- helper: counts as samples x taxa matrix ----
otu_mat <- function(ps) {
  m <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix"); if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) m <- t(m); m
}

# ---- one phyloseq object per week (zero-sum ASVs removed within each week) ----
weeks <- levels(sd$Week)
ps_wk <- map(setNames(weeks, paste0("wk", weeks)), function(w) {
  p <- prune_samples(sample_data(dist.temp.git.ps)$Week == w, dist.temp.git.ps)
  prune_taxa(taxa_sums(p) > 0, p)
})
map_dfr(ps_wk, ~ tibble(samples = nsamples(.x), ASVs = ntaxa(.x),
                        min_depth = min(sample_sums(.x))), .id = "week")
```

```{r}
# ---- Class-level data for one week ----
rare_lab  <- "Rare taxa (< 1%)"
unass_lab <- "Unassigned at Class level"

make_class_data <- function(ps, rare_cut = 0.01) {
  df <- ps %>% tax_glom("Class", NArm = FALSE) %>%
    transform_sample_counts(function(x) x / sum(x)) %>% psmelt()
  df$Class <- ifelse(is.na(df$Class), unass_lab, df$Class)
  df <- df %>% group_by(Sample, Temperature, Week, Class) %>%
    summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop")
  if (!is.null(rare_cut)) {
    keep <- df %>% group_by(Class) %>% summarise(m = mean(Abundance)) %>%
      filter(m >= rare_cut) %>% pull(Class)
    df <- df %>% mutate(Class = ifelse(Class %in% keep, Class, rare_lab)) %>%
      group_by(Sample, Temperature, Week, Class) %>%
      summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop")
  }
  df
}

bar_data <- map(ps_wk, ~ list(rare = make_class_data(.x, 0.01),
                              all  = make_class_data(.x, NULL)))

# ---- colours (same scheme as Field), shared across weeks ----
distinct_palette <- c(
  "#1f78b4", "#FF69B4", "#33a02c", "#ff7f00", "#984ea3", "#e41a1c",
  "#4ea3d9", "#b07cc6", "#66c2a5", "#a65628", "#f781bf", "#238b45",
  "#6a3d9a", "#e6ab02", "#00a6d6", "#d95f02", "#8c6bb1", "#41ae76",
  "#fb6a4a", "#377eb8", "#cab2d6", "#b15928", "#74c476", "#e7298a",
  "#ffd92f", "#006d2c", "#a6cee3", "#d4b9da", "#ff9933", "#7b3294"
)
special_colors <- setNames(c("grey70", "darkblue"), c(rare_lab, unass_lab))

kept_taxa <- sort(setdiff(unique(unlist(map(bar_data, ~ .x$rare$Class))), names(special_colors)))
all_taxa  <- sort(setdiff(unique(unlist(map(bar_data, ~ .x$all$Class))),  names(special_colors)))
rest_taxa <- setdiff(all_taxa, kept_taxa)

# Classes that pass 1% in any week get the first colours (always distinct);
# the remaining Classes (all-taxa plots only) continue through the palette, recycling after 30
pal <- rep(distinct_palette, length.out = length(kept_taxa) + length(rest_taxa))
class_cols <- c(setNames(pal, c(kept_taxa, rest_taxa)), special_colors)
if (length(kept_taxa) > length(distinct_palette))
  warning("More than 30 Classes pass 1% – colours repeat in the rare-grouped plots too")

# legend / stack order: alphabetical, then Unassigned, then Rare taxa
order_classes <- function(x) {
  present <- unique(x)
  factor(x, levels = c(sort(setdiff(present, names(special_colors))),
                       intersect(c(unass_lab, rare_lab), present)))
}

temp_lab  <- labeller(Temperature = function(x) paste0(x, " °C"))
bar_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))

# ---- plot functions ----
plot_mean <- function(df, title, legend_cols = 1) {
  d <- df %>% group_by(Temperature, Class) %>%
    summarise(Abundance = mean(Abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(Class = order_classes(Class))
  ggplot(d, aes(Temperature, Abundance, fill = Class)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = class_cols) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = "Temperature (°C)", y = "Mean relative abundance", title = title) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = legend_cols)) + bar_theme
}

plot_samples <- function(df, title) {
  df <- df %>% mutate(Class = order_classes(Class))
  ggplot(df, aes(Sample, Abundance, fill = Class)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.9) +
    facet_grid(. ~ Temperature, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", labeller = temp_lab) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = class_cols) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative abundance", title = title) +
    bar_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 7))
}

# ---- 3 plots per week ----
bar_plots <- imap(bar_data, function(b, wk) {
  w <- paste("Week", sub("wk", "", wk))
  list(rare    = plot_mean(b$rare, paste(w, "– Class (rare <1% grouped)")),
       all     = plot_mean(b$all,  paste(w, "– Class (all taxa)"), legend_cols = 3),
       samples = plot_samples(b$rare, paste(w, "– Class, all samples (rare <1% grouped)")))
})

walk(bar_plots, ~ walk(.x, print))
```

```{r}
# ---- Phylum-level data for one week ----
unass_lab_phy <- "Unassigned at Phylum level"

make_phylum_data <- function(ps, rare_cut = 0.01) {
  df <- ps %>% tax_glom("Phylum", NArm = FALSE) %>%
    transform_sample_counts(function(x) x / sum(x)) %>% psmelt()
  df$Phylum <- ifelse(is.na(df$Phylum), unass_lab_phy, df$Phylum)
  df <- df %>% group_by(Sample, Temperature, Week, Phylum) %>%
    summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop")
  if (!is.null(rare_cut)) {
    keep <- df %>% group_by(Phylum) %>% summarise(m = mean(Abundance)) %>%
      filter(m >= rare_cut) %>% pull(Phylum)
    df <- df %>% mutate(Phylum = ifelse(Phylum %in% keep, Phylum, rare_lab)) %>%
      group_by(Sample, Temperature, Week, Phylum) %>%
      summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop")
  }
  df
}

bar_data_phy <- map(ps_wk, ~ list(rare = make_phylum_data(.x, 0.01),
                                  all  = make_phylum_data(.x, NULL)))

# ---- colours (same scheme as the Class plots), shared across weeks ----
special_colors_phy <- setNames(c("grey70", "darkblue"), c(rare_lab, unass_lab_phy))

kept_phy  <- sort(setdiff(unique(unlist(map(bar_data_phy, ~ .x$rare$Phylum))), names(special_colors_phy)))
all_phy   <- sort(setdiff(unique(unlist(map(bar_data_phy, ~ .x$all$Phylum))),  names(special_colors_phy)))
rest_phy  <- setdiff(all_phy, kept_phy)

pal_phy <- rep(distinct_palette, length.out = length(kept_phy) + length(rest_phy))
phylum_cols <- c(setNames(pal_phy, c(kept_phy, rest_phy)), special_colors_phy)
if (length(kept_phy) > length(distinct_palette))
  warning("More than 30 Phyla pass 1% – colours repeat in the rare-grouped plots too")

# legend / stack order: alphabetical, then Unassigned, then Rare taxa
order_phyla <- function(x) {
  present <- unique(x)
  factor(x, levels = c(sort(setdiff(present, names(special_colors_phy))),
                       intersect(c(unass_lab_phy, rare_lab), present)))
}

# ---- plot functions ----
plot_mean_phy <- function(df, title, legend_cols = 1) {
  d <- df %>% group_by(Temperature, Phylum) %>%
    summarise(Abundance = mean(Abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(Phylum = order_phyla(Phylum))
  ggplot(d, aes(Temperature, Abundance, fill = Phylum)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = phylum_cols) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = "Temperature (°C)", y = "Mean relative abundance", title = title) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = legend_cols)) + bar_theme
}

plot_samples_phy <- function(df, title) {
  df <- df %>% mutate(Phylum = order_phyla(Phylum))
  ggplot(df, aes(Sample, Abundance, fill = Phylum)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.9) +
    facet_grid(. ~ Temperature, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", labeller = temp_lab) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = phylum_cols) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative abundance", title = title) +
    bar_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 7))
}

# ---- 3 plots per week ----
bar_plots_phy <- imap(bar_data_phy, function(b, wk) {
  w <- paste("Week", sub("wk", "", wk))
  list(rare    = plot_mean_phy(b$rare, paste(w, "– Phylum (rare <1% grouped)")),
       all     = plot_mean_phy(b$all,  paste(w, "– Phylum (all taxa)"), legend_cols = 2),
       samples = plot_samples_phy(b$rare, paste(w, "– Phylum, all samples (rare <1% grouped)")))
})
walk(bar_plots_phy, ~ walk(.x, print))
```

```{r}
make_rarecurve <- function(otu, metadata, depth, title) {
  rc <- vegan::rarecurve(otu, step = 1000, tidy = TRUE)
  rc$Temperature <- metadata[as.character(rc$Site), "Temperature"]
  ggplot(rc, aes(Sample, Species, group = Site, colour = Temperature)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = depth, colour = "grey40", linetype = "dashed") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = temp_colors, name = "Temperature") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
    labs(x = "Sequencing depth (reads)", y = "Observed ASV richness", title = title) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12)
}

rc_wk1 <- make_rarecurve(tempwk1.otu, tempwk1.metadata, 38886, "Week 1")
```

~single & repeated rarefaction for each week, alpha metrics for repeated rarefaction 

```{r}
n_draws <- 100

rarefy_week <- function(ps) {
  depth <- min(sample_sums(ps))
  single <- rarefy_even_depth(ps, sample.size = depth, rngseed = 123,
                              replace = FALSE, trimOTUs = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
  otu <- otu_mat(ps)
  count_sum <- matrix(0, nrow(otu), ncol(otu), dimnames = dimnames(otu))
  alpha_draws <- vector("list", n_draws)
  for (i in seq_len(n_draws)) {
    r <- vegan::rrarefy(otu, depth)
    count_sum <- count_sum + r
    alpha_draws[[i]] <- tibble(SampleID   = rownames(r),
                               Observed   = rowSums(r > 0),
                               Shannon    = vegan::diversity(r, "shannon"),
                               InvSimpson = vegan::diversity(r, "invsimpson")) %>%
      mutate(Pielou = Shannon / log(Observed))
  }
  alpha100 <- bind_rows(alpha_draws) %>% group_by(SampleID) %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), mean), .groups = "drop")
  avg <- round(count_sum / n_draws); avg <- avg[, colSums(avg) > 0]
  rare100 <- phyloseq(otu_table(avg, taxa_are_rows = FALSE), sample_data(ps), tax_table(ps))
  list(depth = depth, single = single, alpha100 = alpha100, rare100 = rare100)
}

rare_wk <- map(ps_wk, rarefy_week)
map_dbl(rare_wk, "depth")     # rarefaction depth used for each week
```

Alpha Diversity - making dataframes (unrare, single rare, repeated rare done above)
```{r}
make_alpha_df <- function(ps) {
  alpha <- estimate_richness(ps, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson"))
  alpha$Sample      <- sample_names(ps)            # avoids make.names() mangling
  md                <- data.frame(sample_data(ps))
  alpha$Temperature <- md[alpha$Sample, "Temperature"]
  alpha$Depth       <- as.numeric(sample_sums(ps)[alpha$Sample])
  alpha$Evenness    <- ifelse(alpha$Observed > 1, alpha$Shannon / log(alpha$Observed), NA)
  rownames(alpha)   <- alpha$Sample
  alpha[, c("Sample","Temperature","Depth",
            "Observed","Shannon","InvSimpson","Evenness")]
}

# averaged over 100 draws, from rare_wk (already calculated per draw, then averaged)
make_alpha_avg <- function(wk, ps) {
  a  <- as.data.frame(rare_wk[[wk]]$alpha100)
  md <- data.frame(sample_data(ps))
  a$Sample      <- a$SampleID
  a$Temperature <- md[a$Sample, "Temperature"]
  a$Depth       <- rare_wk[[wk]]$depth
  a$Evenness    <- ifelse(a$Observed > 1, a$Shannon / log(a$Observed), NA)
  rownames(a)   <- a$Sample
  a[, c("Sample","Temperature","Depth",
        "Observed","Shannon","InvSimpson","Evenness")]
}

# ---- Week 1 ----
alpha_sets_wk1 <- list(unrarefied  = make_alpha_df(temp.wk1.ps),
                       rare_avg    = make_alpha_avg("wk1", temp.wk1.ps),
                       rare_single = make_alpha_df(rare_wk$wk1$single))
# ---- Week 3 ----
alpha_sets_wk3 <- list(unrarefied  = make_alpha_df(temp.wk3.ps),
                       rare_avg    = make_alpha_avg("wk3", temp.wk3.ps),
                       rare_single = make_alpha_df(rare_wk$wk3$single))
# ---- Week 5 ----
alpha_sets_wk5 <- list(unrarefied  = make_alpha_df(temp.wk5.ps),
                       rare_avg    = make_alpha_avg("wk5", temp.wk5.ps),
                       rare_single = make_alpha_df(rare_wk$wk5$single))

# CHECK: 12 samples in each, no lost Temperature labels
check_sets <- function(s) sapply(s, function(d) c(n = nrow(d), NA_temp = sum(is.na(d$Temperature))))
check_sets(alpha_sets_wk1); check_sets(alpha_sets_wk3); check_sets(alpha_sets_wk5)
```

BETA DIVERISTY SET UP - CHECKING FILTERS
~~
Type of Data & Filter Compared Here 

Repeat for Each Week (1,3,5)
1	Unrarefied (12 mats) - 	ASVs present in at least 2! mats
~ a prevalence filter. It drops ASVs found in fewer than 2 mats.
2	Unrarefied (12 mats)	 - purgeOutliers ASV rules (otu.cut 0.0001, zero.cut 0.02), sample step off (sampleZcut = -100)  
~ an abundance filter. It drops ASVs with too few reads in total, wherever they occur.

3	Rarefied (100-draw average, 
Week 1: 38,886 reads
Week 3: 29,841 reads
Week 5: 38,367 reads
reads) - 	No filter

*All three use CLR with a pseudocount of 1, then Euclidean distance (Aitchison).

for filter (1) how many reads is it actually removing?
```{r}
map_dfr(c(wk1 = "wk1", wk3 = "wk3", wk5 = "wk5"), function(wk) {
  ps   <- ps_wk[[wk]]
  prev <- colSums(otu_mat(ps) > 0)
  keep <- prev >= 3
  tibble(ASVs_total   = length(prev),
         ASVs_kept    = sum(keep),
         pct_ASVs     = round(100 * mean(keep), 1),
         pct_reads    = round(100 * sum(taxa_sums(ps)[keep]) / sum(taxa_sums(ps)), 1))
}, .id = "week")
```

dist.field.git.ps
temp.wk1.ps
temp.wk3.ps

```{r}
prev_check <- function(ps, cutoffs = c(2, 3)) {
  m <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix"); if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) m <- t(m)   # samples x ASVs
  m <- m[, colSums(m) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  prev  <- colSums(m > 0)
  reads <- colSums(m)
  map_dfr(cutoffs, function(k) tibble(
    samples    = nrow(m),
    cutoff     = paste0(">= ", k, " mats"),
    ASVs_total = length(prev),
    ASVs_kept  = sum(prev >= k),
    pct_ASVs   = round(100 * mean(prev >= k), 1),
    pct_reads  = round(100 * sum(reads[prev >= k]) / sum(reads), 1)
  ))
}

bind_rows(
  prev_check(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.ps) %>% mutate(set = "Summer wk5 (no HD)"),
  prev_check(dist.field.git.ps)        %>% mutate(set = "Field"),
  prev_check(temp.wk1.ps)              %>% mutate(set = "Temp wk1"),
  prev_check(temp.wk3.ps)              %>% mutate(set = "Temp wk3"),
  prev_check(temp.wk5.ps)              %>% mutate(set = "Temp wk5")
) %>% relocate(set)

```
Lab Dist and Field: keep ≥ 3 mats. The filter keeps 94–96% of reads and only removes the rare tail.

Temp:
  - do ≥ 2 mats. 
  - At ≥ 3  lose 12–16% of reads (84–88% kept), which is noticeably more than in the other experiments. 
  - At ≥ 2  keep 92–94%, close to Lab Dist and Field.

```{r}
## ---------- 0. purgeOutliers: get it once, then load it locally ----------
if (!file.exists("purgeOutliers.R")) {
  tmp <- tempdir()
  download.file("https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/MCMC.OTU/MCMC.OTU_1.0.10.tar.gz",
                destfile = file.path(tmp, "MCMC.OTU.tar.gz"), mode = "wb")
  untar(file.path(tmp, "MCMC.OTU.tar.gz"), exdir = tmp)
  file.copy(file.path(tmp, "MCMC.OTU", "R", "purgeOutliers.R"), "purgeOutliers.R")
}
source("purgeOutliers.R")

## ---------- helper: quick summary of what a filter kept ----------
filter_summary <- function(before, after) {
  c(ASVs_before = ntaxa(before),
    ASVs_after  = ntaxa(after),
    samples     = nsamples(after),
    pct_reads   = round(sum(taxa_sums(after)) /
                        sum(taxa_sums(prune_samples(sample_names(after), before))) * 100, 2))
}
```

```{r}
## ---------- 1. MAIN: prevalence filter (ASV in >= 2 of 12 mats) ----------
temp.wk1.filt.ps <- filter_taxa(temp.wk1.ps, function(x) sum(x > 0) >= 2, prune = TRUE)
## ---------- 2. SENSITIVITY 1: purgeOutliers ASV rules ----------
otu.mat <- as(otu_table(temp.wk1.ps), "matrix")
if (taxa_are_rows(temp.wk1.ps)) otu.mat <- t(otu.mat)       # samples x ASVs

seq.formcmc <- data.frame(X = seq_len(nrow(otu.mat)),
                          sample = rownames(otu.mat),
                          otu.mat, check.names = FALSE)

seq.trim.allinfo <- purgeOutliers(seq.formcmc,
                                  count.columns = 3:ncol(seq.formcmc),
                                  sampleZcut = -100,          # keep all 12 mats
                                  otu.cut = 0.0001, zero.cut = 0.02)

temp.wk1.purged.ps <- prune_taxa(colnames(seq.trim.allinfo)[-(1:2)], temp.wk1.ps)
temp.wk1.purged.ps <- prune_samples(seq.trim.allinfo$sample, temp.wk1.purged.ps)
## ---------- 3. SENSITIVITY 2: unfiltered, 100-draw averaged rarefied ----------
temp.wk1.rareavg.ps <- rare_wk$wk1$rare100     # built in the rarefaction chunk (38,886 reads)
```

BETA DISPERSION/ DIVERSITY
~
function to repeat
```{r}
run_beta <- function(ps, n_perm = 9999) {
  # ASV table (samples as rows) + matching metadata
  otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
  if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)
  md <- data.frame(sample_data(ps))[rownames(otu), , drop = FALSE]

  # CLR by hand (pseudocount 1) -> Euclidean = Aitchison distance
  clr <- log(otu + 1)
  clr <- clr - rowMeans(clr)
  d   <- vegdist(clr, method = "euclidean")
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(md), labels(d)))

  # Dispersion by Temperature
  set.seed(123)
  disp <- betadisper(d, md$Temperature, bias.adjust = TRUE)

  # One-way PERMANOVA
  set.seed(123)
  perm <- adonis2(d ~ Temperature, data = md, permutations = n_perm)

  list(clr = clr, dist = d, md = md, betadisper = disp,
       disp_anova = anova(disp),
       disp_perm  = permutest(disp, pairwise = TRUE, permutations = n_perm),
       permanova  = perm)
}
```

PCOA PLOTS

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)

temp_colors <- c("26" = "blue3", "29" = "green3", "31" = "pink3", "33" = "red4")

make_pcoa_plot <- function(beta, ps, title) {
  stopifnot(ncol(beta$clr) == ntaxa(ps))                      # same ASVs as the filtered object
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(beta$md), labels(beta$dist)))  # same sample order

  pcoa    <- ape::pcoa(beta$dist)
  percent <- round(pcoa$values$Relative_eig * 100, 1)
  df <- cbind(data.frame(PCoA1 = pcoa$vectors[, 1],
                         PCoA2 = pcoa$vectors[, 2]),
              beta$md)

  # shaded area around each temperature's 3 points (convex hull)
  hulls <- df %>% group_by(Temperature) %>% slice(chull(PCoA1, PCoA2))

  perm <- beta$permanova
  perm_label <- sprintf("Temperature: R² = %.3f, p = %.3f", perm$R2[1], perm$`Pr(>F)`[1])

  ggplot(df, aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, color = Temperature)) +
    geom_polygon(data = hulls, aes(group = Temperature, fill = Temperature),
                 alpha = 0.15, color = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_point(size = 3.5, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_color_manual(values = temp_colors, name = "Temperature (°C)") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = temp_colors) +
    annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.5, size = 3,
             label = perm_label) +
    labs(title = title,
         x = paste0("PCoA 1 (", percent[1], "%)"),
         y = paste0("PCoA 2 (", percent[2], "%)")) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))
}

pcoa.wk1 <- make_pcoa_plot(beta.wk1.filt, temp.wk1.filt.ps, "Week 1")
pcoa.wk3 <- make_pcoa_plot(beta.wk3.filt, temp.wk3.filt.ps, "Week 3")
pcoa.wk5 <- make_pcoa_plot(beta.wk5.filt, temp.wk5.filt.ps, "Week 5")

# one shared legend on the right

temp.pcoa.panel <- plot_grid(
  pcoa.wk1 + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  pcoa.wk3 + theme(legend.position = "none"),
```

In Week 3 the PERMANOVA is significant, so the community as a whole differs by temperature. But no named Class changes enough on its own to be flagged. So the shift is probably spread out, and it can come from two places:
- Small changes across many Classes, none big enough to pass ANCOM-BC2 with n = 3 per group.
- Changes at the ASV level inside Classes. Your beta diversity is ASV-level, but ANCOM-BC2 is Class-level.
- If some ASVs in a Class go up while others go down, the Class total can stay about the same.

```{r}
#looking at all significant results at once 
tidy_ancom <- function(a, week) {
  pattern <- "^(lfc|se|W|p|q|diff|passed_ss)_(Temperature.*)$"

  relabel <- function(x) {
    x <- gsub("Temperature", "", x)
    ifelse(grepl("_", x), sub("_", " vs ", x), paste(x, "vs 26"))
  }

  dunn <- a$res_dunn %>%
    select(taxon, matches(pattern)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-taxon, names_to = c(".value", "comparison"), names_pattern = pattern) %>%
    mutate(test = "Dunnett")

  pair <- a$res_pair %>%
    select(taxon, matches(pattern)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-taxon, names_to = c(".value", "comparison"), names_pattern = pattern) %>%
    mutate(test = "Pairwise")

  glob <- a$res_global %>%
    select(taxon, any_of(c("W", "p_val", "q_val", "diff_abn", "passed_ss"))) %>%
    rename(any_of(c(p = "p_val", q = "q_val", diff = "diff_abn"))) %>%
    mutate(comparison = "global", test = "Global")

  bind_rows(glob, dunn, pair) %>%
    mutate(week = week,
           comparison = ifelse(comparison == "global", "global", relabel(comparison)),
           fold_change = round(exp(lfc), 2),
           direction = case_when(is.na(lfc) ~ NA_character_,
                                 lfc > 0 ~ "higher in 1st", TRUE ~ "lower in 1st")) %>%
    select(week, test, taxon, comparison, lfc, fold_change, direction, se, q, diff, any_of("passed_ss"))
}

# ---- sensitivity scores in long format, one row per taxon x comparison ----
# key = the two temperatures sorted (e.g. "26-33"), or "global"
make_key <- function(x) {
  map_chr(x, function(s) {
    t <- as.numeric(unlist(str_extract_all(s, "\\d+")))
    if (length(t) == 0) return("global")
    if (length(t) == 1) t <- c(26, t)            # "Temperature33" means 33 vs 26
    paste(sort(t), collapse = "-")
  })
}

tidy_sens <- function(a, week) {
  a$pseudo_sens_tab %>%
    select(-any_of("(Intercept)")) %>%
    pivot_longer(-taxon, names_to = "col", values_to = "sens_score") %>%
    mutate(week = week, key = make_key(col)) %>%
    distinct(week, taxon, key, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%   # vs-26 scores appear twice, identical
    select(week, taxon, key, sens_score)
}

sens_long <- bind_rows(
  tidy_sens(ancom.tempwk1, "wk1"),
  tidy_sens(ancom.tempwk3, "wk3"),
  tidy_sens(ancom.tempwk5, "wk5")
)

# ---- all results + sensitivity score ----
ancom_all <- bind_rows(
  tidy_ancom(ancom.tempwk1, "wk1"),
  tidy_ancom(ancom.tempwk3, "wk3"),
  tidy_ancom(ancom.tempwk5, "wk5")
) %>%
  mutate(key = ifelse(comparison == "global", "global", make_key(comparison))) %>%
  left_join(sens_long, by = c("week", "taxon", "key")) %>%
  select(-key)

# only the significant hits
ancom_sig <- ancom_all %>% filter(diff) %>% arrange(week, test, taxon, comparison)

print(ancom_sig, n = Inf, width = Inf)          # prints every row and column
write.csv(ancom_sig, "ancom_temp_sig_hits.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(ancom_all, "ancom_temp_all_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

The story across weeks:
Week 1: one Class differs (Deinococci, higher at 31 °C).
Week 3: no named Classes differ. The community shift is spread across many small changes.
Week 5: 7 Classes differ, and almost all involve 33 °C. Campylobacteria and 028H05-P-BN-P5 decline, while Fimbriimonadia, Dadabacteriia and two CPR Classes (Gracilibacteria and Parcubacteria) increase.

```{r}
library(car)
temppam$Temperature <- as.factor(temppam$Temperature)
temppam$Week        <- as.factor(temppam$Week)

table(temppam$Week, temppam$Temperature)   # mats per temperature in each week

run_pam_week <- function(wk) {
  d <- subset(temppam, Week == wk)
  d <- droplevels(d)
  cat("\n================ WEEK", wk, "( n =", nrow(d), ") ================\n")

  fit <- aov(pam ~ Temperature, data = d)
  print(summary(fit))

  # 1. Normality
  qqnorm(residuals(fit), main = paste("Week", wk, "Q-Q plot"))
  qqline(residuals(fit), col = "red")
  print(shapiro.test(residuals(fit)))

  # 2. Homogeneity
  print(leveneTest(pam ~ Temperature, data = d))

  # 3. Residuals vs fitted
  plot(fit, which = 1, main = paste("Week", wk))

  # effect size
  tab <- summary(fit)[[1]]
  tab$eta_sq <- round(tab$`Sum Sq` / sum(tab$`Sum Sq`), 3)
  print(tab)

  # post hoc only if significant
  if (summary(fit)[[1]]$`Pr(>F)`[1] < 0.05) print(TukeyHSD(fit))

  invisible(fit)
}

pam.wk1 <- run_pam_week("1")
pam.wk2 <- run_pam_week("2")
pam.wk3 <- run_pam_week("3")
pam.wk4 <- run_pam_week("4")
pam.wk5 <- run_pam_week("5")
```
```{r}
pam_summary <- map_dfr(c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"), function(wk) {
  d   <- droplevels(subset(temppam, Week == wk))
  fit <- aov(pam ~ Temperature, data = d)
  tab <- summary(fit)[[1]]
  tibble(
    Week      = wk,
    n         = nrow(d),
    F         = round(tab$`F value`[1], 2),
    df        = paste0(tab$Df[1], ", ", tab$Df[2]),
    p         = signif(tab$`Pr(>F)`[1], 3),
    eta_sq    = round(tab$`Sum Sq`[1] / sum(tab$`Sum Sq`), 3),
    shapiro_p = signif(shapiro.test(residuals(fit))$p.value, 3),
    levene_p  = signif(leveneTest(pam ~ Temperature, data = d)$`Pr(>F)`[1], 3)
  )
}) %>%
  mutate(p_holm = signif(p.adjust(p, method = "holm"), 3))   # adjusted across the 5 weeks

pam_summary
#write.csv(pam_summary, "temp_pam_by_week.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

TOM first
```{r}
tempnutsdiff$Temperature <- as.factor(tempnutsdiff$Temperature)
tom1 <- aov(W5.W1...OM. ~ Temperature, data = tempnutsdiff)
summary(tom1)

#assumption check
#1. Normality
qqnorm(residuals(tom1))
qqline(residuals(tom1), col = "red")
shapiro_test <- shapiro.test(residuals(tom1))
print(shapiro_test)
#2. Homogeneity
library(car)
tempnutsdiff$Temperature <- as.character(tempnutsdiff$Temperature)
levene_test <- leveneTest(W5.W1...OM. ~ Temperature, data = tempnutsdiff)
print(levene_test)
#3 linearity
plot(tom1, which = 1)
plot
#4 independence (think about sample design)
durbinWatsonTest(tom1)
```
*no stat diff, assumptions good

combo pam & nutrient plot
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)

temp_fill <- c("26" = "blue3", "29" = "green3", "31" = "pink3", "33" = "red4")

nut_theme <- theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
        legend.position = "right",
        plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5))

# ---- Y(II): weeks 1, 4, 5 ----
pam145 <- subset(temppam, Week %in% c("1", "4", "5"))
pam145$Temperature <- factor(pam145$Temperature, levels = c("26", "29", "31", "33"))
pam145$Week        <- factor(pam145$Week, levels = c("1", "4", "5"))

pam.plot <- ggplot(pam145, aes(x = Temperature, y = pam,
                               fill = Temperature, shape = Week,
                               group = interaction(Temperature, Week))) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.6, colour = "black",
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1, dodge.width = 0.8),
             colour = "black", size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = temp_fill, guide = "none") +          # x-axis already shows temperature
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("1" = 16, "4" = 17, "5" = 15)) +   # circle, triangle, square
  labs(x = "Temperature (°C)", y = "Y(II)", shape = "Week") +
  nut_theme

# ---- %TN difference (legend removed so the panels line up) ----
nuts6.1 <- ggplot(tempnutsdiff, aes(x = factor(Temperature), y = W5.W1...N.,
                                    fill = factor(Temperature))) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.6, colour = "black", width = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(colour = "black", width = 0.15, alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.3, 0.1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = temp_fill, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Temperature (°C)", y = "%TN Difference") +
  nut_theme

# ---- stacked panel ----
pam.nuts.panel <- plot_grid(pam.plot, nuts6.1, ncol = 1,
                            labels = c("A", "B"), align = "v", axis = "lr")
pam.nuts.panel
```

sample stats
```{r}
library(phyloseq)

weeks <- sort(unique(sample_data(dist.temp.git.ps)$Week))  # change "Week" if your column is named differently

temp_week_stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(weeks, function(w) {
  ps_w <- prune_samples(sample_data(dist.temp.git.ps)$Week == w, dist.temp.git.ps)
  ps_w <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_w) > 0, ps_w)   # keep only ASVs present in this week
  depth <- sample_sums(ps_w)
  data.frame(
    Week      = w,
    n_samples = nsamples(ps_w),
    n_ASVs    = ntaxa(ps_w),
    min_reads = min(depth),
    max_reads = max(depth),
    total_reads = sum(depth)
  )
}))

temp_week_stats

# Ready-to-paste sentences
with(temp_week_stats, sprintf(
  "Week %s: %d samples; %s ASVs, between %s and %s reads/sample",
  Week, n_samples, format(n_ASVs, big.mark = ","),
  format(min_reads, big.mark = ","), format(max_reads, big.mark = ",")
))
```
